# `kernel/SecurityDoctor.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/SecurityDoctor.js`

SecurityDoctor.js — in-browser security posture report (no Node required). Aggregates the OS's runtime security signals into a single graded report: - syscall guard coverage (reuses auditSyscallGuards) - complete capability-policy coverage (reuses auditCapabilityMap) - permission enforcement state - package trust posture (quarantined / untrusted installed packages) - update supply-chain policy (signed + trusted-for-auto) - GPU containment (per-app broker + VRAM quotas) - shell CSP delivery (Report-Only vs enforcing, inline-script regressions) - browser-extension presence Each finding has a severity ('critical'|'high'|'medium'|'low'|'info') and a pass flag. `runSecurityDoctor(kernel)` returns a structured report suitable for logging or rendering in a Security Doctor panel.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
